## RANGE values and functions
# Sources: BigQuery's range-functions examples, data-types#range_type and lexical#range_literals;
# its comparable data types notes on RANGE; conversion_functions#cast_as_range. A RANGE<DATE> is
# returned as "[start, end)", with UNBOUNDED for a missing bound, as the client libraries parse it.

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2020-12-31)'
=> "[2020-01-01, 2020-12-31)"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[UNBOUNDED, 2020-12-31)'
=> "[UNBOUNDED, 2020-12-31)"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[NULL, 2020-12-31)'
=> "[UNBOUNDED, 2020-12-31)"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)'
=> "[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)"

# Without formatOptions.useInt64Timestamp, the bounds of a RANGE<TIMESTAMP> are seconds with six
# fractional digits, even for a whole second; confirmed against BigQuery.
SELECT RANGE<TIMESTAMP> '[2020-01-01 00:00:00.5+00, UNBOUNDED)'
=> "[1577836800.500000, UNBOUNDED)"

SELECT RANGE<TIMESTAMP> '[2020-01-01 00:00:00+00, 2021-01-01 00:00:00+00)'
=> "[1577836800.000000, 1609459200.000000)"

SELECT RANGE<TIMESTAMP> '[1969-12-31 23:59:59.5+00, UNBOUNDED)'
=> "[-0.500000, UNBOUNDED)"

# CAST to STRING writes each bound cast to STRING, and UNBOUNDED for a missing one; confirmed
# against BigQuery.
SELECT CAST(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)' AS STRING)
=> "[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)"

SELECT CAST(RANGE<DATETIME> '[UNBOUNDED, 2021-01-01 12:30:00)' AS STRING)
=> "[UNBOUNDED, 2021-01-01 12:30:00)"

SELECT CAST(RANGE<TIMESTAMP> '[2020-01-01 01:02:03.5+00, 2021-01-01 00:00:00+00)' AS STRING)
=> "[2020-01-01 01:02:03.500+00, 2021-01-01 00:00:00+00)"

SELECT CAST(NULL AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> null

SELECT RANGE(DATE '2022-12-01', DATE '2022-12-31')
=> "[2022-12-01, 2022-12-31)"

SELECT RANGE(NULL, DATE '2022-12-31')
=> "[UNBOUNDED, 2022-12-31)"

SELECT RANGE(DATE '2022-10-01', NULL)
=> "[2022-10-01, UNBOUNDED)"

# The lower bound must be smaller than the upper bound; SAFE. returns NULL instead. BigQuery's
# message is confirmed against BigQuery.
SELECT RANGE(DATE '2022-12-31', DATE '2022-12-01')
=> error: Range start element must be smaller than range end element; error in RANGE expression

SELECT RANGE(DATE '2022-12-01', DATE '2022-12-01')
=> error:

SELECT SAFE.RANGE(DATE '2022-12-31', DATE '2022-12-01')
=> null

SELECT IF(FALSE, RANGE(DATE '2022-12-31', DATE '2022-12-01'), NULL)
=> null

SELECT RANGE_START(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-12-01, 2022-12-31)')
=> "2022-12-01"

SELECT RANGE_START(RANGE<DATE> '[UNBOUNDED, 2022-12-31)')
=> null

SELECT RANGE_START(CAST(NULL AS RANGE<DATE>))
=> null

SELECT RANGE_END(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-12-01, 2022-12-31)')
=> "2022-12-31"

SELECT RANGE_END(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-12-01, UNBOUNDED)')
=> null

SELECT RANGE_END(CAST(NULL AS RANGE<DATE>))
=> null

SELECT RANGE_CONTAINS(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-01-01, 2023-01-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2022-04-01, 2022-07-01)')
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE_CONTAINS(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-01-01, 2023-01-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2023-01-01, 2023-04-01)')
=> "false"

SELECT RANGE_CONTAINS(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-01-01, 2023-01-01)', DATE '2022-04-01')
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE_CONTAINS(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-01-01, 2023-01-01)', DATE '2023-04-01')
=> "false"

SELECT RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-02-01, 2022-09-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, 2022-04-15)')
=> "[2022-02-01, 2022-04-15)"

SELECT RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-02-01, UNBOUNDED)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, 2022-04-15)')
=> "[2022-02-01, 2022-04-15)"

SELECT RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-02-01, UNBOUNDED)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, UNBOUNDED)')
=> "[2022-02-01, UNBOUNDED)"

SELECT RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-02-01, UNBOUNDED)', CAST(NULL AS RANGE<DATE>))
=> null

# Ranges that do not overlap are an error; SAFE. returns NULL instead.
SELECT RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-02-01, 2020-09-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, 2022-04-15)')
=> error:

SELECT SAFE.RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-02-01, 2020-09-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, 2022-04-15)')
=> null

# BigQuery's message, confirmed against BigQuery, leaves out the ranges.
SELECT RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-02-01, 2020-09-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, UNBOUNDED)')
=> error: Provided RANGE inputs do not overlap. Please check RANGE_OVERLAPS before calling RANGE_INTERSECT; error in RANGE_INTERSECT expression

SELECT RANGE_OVERLAPS(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-02-01, 2022-09-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, 2022-04-15)')
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE_OVERLAPS(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-02-01, 2020-09-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, 2022-04-15)')
=> "false"

SELECT RANGE_OVERLAPS(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-02-01, UNBOUNDED)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, UNBOUNDED)')
=> "true"

# Ranges compare by their lower bounds, then by their upper bounds. A NULL lower bound sorts
# before the others, a NULL upper bound after them, and two NULL bounds are equal.
SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[UNBOUNDED, 2020-01-01)' < RANGE<DATE> '[2019-01-01, 2020-01-01)'
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)' > RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2021-01-01)'
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2021-01-01)' < RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-02, 2020-01-03)'
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[UNBOUNDED, UNBOUNDED)' = RANGE(CAST(NULL AS DATE), NULL)
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2021-01-01)' = CAST(NULL AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> null

SELECT ARRAY(
  SELECT r FROM UNNEST([
    RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)', RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2020-02-01)',
    RANGE<DATE> '[UNBOUNDED, 2021-01-01)']) AS r
  ORDER BY r)
=> [{"v": "[UNBOUNDED, 2021-01-01)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-01, 2020-02-01)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)"}]

SELECT CAST('[2020-01-01, 2020-01-02)' AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> "[2020-01-01, 2020-01-02)"

SELECT CAST(CONCAT('[2020-01-01, ', '2020-01-02)') AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> "[2020-01-01, 2020-01-02)"

SELECT CAST(CONCAT('[UNBOUNDED, ', '2020-01-02)') AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> "[UNBOUNDED, 2020-01-02)"

SELECT CAST(CONCAT('[2020-01-01, ', 'NULL)') AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> "[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)"

SELECT CAST(CONCAT('[2020-01-01, ', NULL) AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> null

# The text must have the range literal format.
SELECT CAST(CONCAT('[2020-01-01,', '2020-01-02)') AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> error:

SELECT CAST(CONCAT('(2020-01-01, ', '2020-01-02)') AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> error:

SELECT CAST(CONCAT('[2020-01-02, ', '2020-01-01)') AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> error:

# GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY: BigQuery's range-functions examples, and NULL for any NULL argument.
SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE(DATE '2020-01-01', DATE '2020-01-06'), INTERVAL 1 DAY)
=> [{"v": "[2020-01-01, 2020-01-02)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-02, 2020-01-03)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-03, 2020-01-04)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-04, 2020-01-05)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-05, 2020-01-06)"}]

SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE(DATE '2020-01-01', DATE '2020-01-06'), INTERVAL 2 DAY)
=> [{"v": "[2020-01-01, 2020-01-03)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-03, 2020-01-05)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-05, 2020-01-06)"}]

SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE(DATE '2020-01-01', DATE '2020-01-06'), INTERVAL 2 DAY, TRUE)
=> [{"v": "[2020-01-01, 2020-01-03)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-03, 2020-01-05)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-05, 2020-01-06)"}]

SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE(DATE '2020-01-01', DATE '2020-01-06'), INTERVAL 2 DAY, FALSE)
=> [{"v": "[2020-01-01, 2020-01-03)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-03, 2020-01-05)"}]

SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(CAST(NULL AS RANGE<DATE>), INTERVAL 1 DAY) IS NULL
=> "true"

SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE(DATE '2020-01-01', DATE '2020-01-06'), CAST(NULL AS INTERVAL)) IS NULL
=> "true"

SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE(DATE '2020-01-01', DATE '2020-01-06'), INTERVAL 1 DAY, NULL) IS NULL
=> "true"

# Steps of other parts and element types; GoogleSQL's compliance test data.
SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-02-24, 2020-03-24)', INTERVAL 7 DAY, FALSE)
=> [{"v": "[2020-02-24, 2020-03-02)"}, {"v": "[2020-03-02, 2020-03-09)"}, {"v": "[2020-03-09, 2020-03-16)"}, {"v": "[2020-03-16, 2020-03-23)"}]

SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-04-30, 2020-08-24)', INTERVAL 1 MONTH)
=> [{"v": "[2020-04-30, 2020-05-30)"}, {"v": "[2020-05-30, 2020-06-30)"}, {"v": "[2020-06-30, 2020-07-30)"}, {"v": "[2020-07-30, 2020-08-24)"}]

SELECT ARRAY_TO_STRING(ARRAY(SELECT CAST(r AS STRING) FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(
  RANGE<DATETIME> '[2023-04-24 08:20:37, 2023-04-25 08:21:37)', INTERVAL 8 HOUR)) AS r), ' ')
=> "[2023-04-24 08:20:37, 2023-04-24 16:20:37) [2023-04-24 16:20:37, 2023-04-25 00:20:37) [2023-04-25 00:20:37, 2023-04-25 08:20:37) [2023-04-25 08:20:37, 2023-04-25 08:21:37)"

SELECT ARRAY_TO_STRING(ARRAY(SELECT CAST(r AS STRING) FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(
  RANGE<TIMESTAMP> '[2023-04-24 08:20:37+00, 2023-04-25 08:21:37+00)', INTERVAL 8 HOUR, FALSE)) AS r), ' ')
=> "[2023-04-24 08:20:37+00, 2023-04-24 16:20:37+00) [2023-04-24 16:20:37+00, 2023-04-25 00:20:37+00) [2023-04-25 00:20:37+00, 2023-04-25 08:20:37+00)"

# Answers from BigQuery: GoogleSQL's errors, named after the function, and steps of parts below
# SECOND or of more than one part.
SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)', INTERVAL 1 DAY)
=> error: input RANGE cannot have UNBOUNDED endpoints; error in GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY expression

SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2020-01-06)', INTERVAL 0 DAY)
=> error: step cannot be 0; error in GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY expression

SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2020-01-06)', INTERVAL -1 DAY)
=> error: step cannot be negative; error in GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY expression

SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE<TIMESTAMP> '[2020-01-01 00:00:00+00, 2020-03-01 00:00:00+00)', INTERVAL 1 MONTH)
=> error: step with non-zero MONTH or YEAR part is not supported; error in GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY expression

SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2020-01-06)', INTERVAL 12 HOUR)
=> error: step with non-zero (H:M:S[.F]) part is not supported; error in GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY expression

SELECT SAFE.GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2020-01-06)', INTERVAL 0 DAY) IS NULL
=> "true"

SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE<TIMESTAMP> '[2020-01-01 00:00:00+00, 2020-01-01 00:00:01+00)', INTERVAL 500 MILLISECOND)
=> [{"v": "[1577836800.000000, 1577836800.500000)"}, {"v": "[1577836800.500000, 1577836801.000000)"}]

SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE<DATETIME> '[2020-01-01 00:00:00, 2020-01-03 00:00:00)', INTERVAL '1 2' DAY TO HOUR)
=> [{"v": "[2020-01-01T00:00:00, 2020-01-02T02:00:00)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-02T02:00:00, 2020-01-03T00:00:00)"}]

# A MONTH step adds to the start, so a subrange after one clamped to the end of a shorter month
# ends on the start's day again.
SELECT GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-31, 2020-05-24)', INTERVAL 1 MONTH)
=> [{"v": "[2020-01-31, 2020-02-29)"}, {"v": "[2020-02-29, 2020-03-31)"}, {"v": "[2020-03-31, 2020-04-30)"}, {"v": "[2020-04-30, 2020-05-24)"}]

# JSON encodes a RANGE as an object of its start and end, with null for an unbounded end; the
# documented SQL-to-JSON encoding table, with each bound encoded as a value of its element type.
SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(RANGE<DATE> '[2024-07-24, 2024-07-25)')
=> "{\"start\":\"2024-07-24\",\"end\":\"2024-07-25\"}"

SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(RANGE<DATETIME> '[2024-07-24 10:00:00, UNBOUNDED)')
=> "{\"start\":\"2024-07-24T10:00:00\",\"end\":null}"

SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(RANGE<TIMESTAMP> '[UNBOUNDED, 2017-03-06 12:34:56.789012+00)')
=> "{\"start\":null,\"end\":\"2017-03-06T12:34:56.789012Z\"}"

SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(CAST(NULL AS RANGE<DATE>))
=> "null"

SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT([RANGE<DATE> '[2024-07-24, UNBOUNDED)'] AS r))
=> "{\"r\":[{\"start\":\"2024-07-24\",\"end\":null}]}"

SELECT STRING(TO_JSON(RANGE<DATE> '[2024-07-24, 2024-07-25)').start)
=> "2024-07-24"

SELECT JSON_TYPE(TO_JSON(RANGE<DATETIME> '[2024-07-24 10:00:00, UNBOUNDED)').`end`)
=> "null"

SELECT STRING(JSON_ARRAY(RANGE<DATE> '[2024-07-24, 2024-07-25)')[0].`end`)
=> "2024-07-25"

SELECT STRING(JSON_OBJECT('r', RANGE<DATE> '[2024-07-24, 2024-07-25)').r.start)
=> "2024-07-24"

SELECT STRING(JSON_SET(JSON '{}', '$.r', RANGE<DATE> '[2024-07-24, 2024-07-25)').r.start)
=> "2024-07-24"

SELECT STRING(JSON_ARRAY_APPEND(JSON '[]', '$', RANGE<DATE> '[2024-07-24, 2024-07-25)')[0].start)
=> "2024-07-24"

SELECT JSON_TYPE(JSON_ARRAY_INSERT(JSON '[]', '$[0]', RANGE<DATE> '[UNBOUNDED, 2024-07-25)')[0].start)
=> "null"
